summary: Shopfloor is a monolithic Node.js e-commerce demo divided into 10 service districts under demo/shopfloor/src/. A single HTTP gateway (gateway) receives all requests and delegates to auth, cart, checkout, inventory, payment, and notifications. State is backed by an in-memory document store (db). The critical path is POST /checkout → CheckoutService.placeOrder → InventoryService.reserve → PaymentService.charge → CardGatewayClient.charge (external PSP simulation) → NotificationService.orderConfirmed.

services.name: Auth
services.responsibility: Authenticates users via password or SSO and manages the session lifecycle. Provides AuthService for credential validation and session creation, and SessionStore for in-memory session persistence.

services.name: Cart
services.responsibility: Manages per-customer shopping carts in memory, supporting item addition with stock validation, total calculation, and cart clearing. Reads product records from the db district.

services.name: Checkout
services.responsibility: Orchestrates the order placement workflow: validates the cart, reserves inventory, charges the customer, clears the cart, and dispatches confirmation or failure notifications. All coordination happens inside CheckoutService.placeOrder.

services.name: Customer
services.responsibility: Loads and caches customer profiles (including billing information) from the database. CustomerService provides getBillingProfile for payment and loadProfile for session hydration.

services.name: DB
services.responsibility: Provides an in-memory document store (DbClient) with findById, findOne, upsert, and update operations, plus a seed function that populates users, customer profiles, and stock inventory on startup.

services.name: Gateway
services.responsibility: The HTTP server entry point: registers all routes (auth, cart, checkout), applies request-id and session-authentication middleware, wires up all service instances, and maps errors to HTTP status codes.

services.name: Inventory
services.responsibility: Tracks available stock per SKU and manages reservation and release operations to prevent overselling. InventoryService.reserve blocks checkout if stock is insufficient and InventoryService.release rolls back on payment failure.

services.name: Notifications
services.responsibility: Queues transactional outbound emails for order confirmation and payment failure events. NotificationService maintains an outbox so that SMTP failures never block the checkout critical path.

services.name: Payment
services.responsibility: Resolves the customer's stored card token, converts the order amount to minor currency units, and delegates to CardGatewayClient which simulates an external PSP with retry-on-timeout logic.

services.name: Shared
services.responsibility: Cross-cutting utilities: HTTP error hierarchy (HttpError, PaymentDeclinedError, OutOfStockError, UnauthorizedError), a structured logger with pluggable sink and clock, and TypeScript domain interfaces (Session, Cart, Order, BillingProfile, etc.).

entryPoints.description: Factory function that seeds the database, wires all service instances, registers all HTTP routes (POST /auth/login, POST /auth/sso/callback, GET /cart, POST /cart/items, POST /checkout), and returns a { handle, notifications } object.
POST /checkout route — authenticates the session then delegates to CheckoutService.placeOrder.
POST /auth/login route — accepts email+password and returns a sessionId cookie.
POST /auth/sso/callback route — accepts an SSO assertion and creates a session.

dataFlows.name: POST /checkout → Card Processor
dataFlows.description: End-to-end order placement flow. The HTTP gateway authenticates the session, then CheckoutService.placeOrder coordinates: (1) cart retrieval, (2) inventory reservation, (3) PaymentService.charge which resolves the stored card token and calls CardGatewayClient.charge (external PSP simulation with 2-attempt retry), (4) cart clear, (5) confirmation email enqueued. On any error after reservation, inventory is released and a paymentFailed email is enqueued.

dataFlows.name: POST /auth/login → Session Created
dataFlows.description: Password-based login flow. The gateway receives email+password, AuthService looks up the user in db, validates the fakeHash, creates a session via SessionStore, hydrates the customer profile, and returns a sessionId.
